artifacts.summary: Implementation summary for the advisory --gate verification tier: core flag plumbing, docs and metadata schema, the books-gate.sh wrapper and its fixture suite, the books agent/skill binding, and core test coverage.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added an advisory-only --gate flag to /orchestrate that, at implement dispatch only, runs the consuming repository's regex layer lint plus a Books.Meta import-closure check via a new extension-local books-gate.sh wrapper (one JSON object, always exit 0, vacuous passes reported as vacuous). Threaded through the full --compare surface in core, documented at all four layers including a new ### gate (optional) metadata schema section, bound in both books implementation agents and both books skills, and pinned by a 44-assertion fixture suite with seven forgery probes plus new Group 17 and Group 35 in the two core suites. A core redeploy is required for --gate to exist at all in any consuming repository, since every edit landed in the source store; enabling the books extension in a consuming repository's .claude-extensions.json remains the user's own action.

memory_candidates.content: A shell lint whose [ok] line reports module/import counts but never RULE APPLICABILITY cannot distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'nothing was checked' by exit code or output. Detect vacuity by sourcing the real rule-set library in a SUBSHELL (never a copy of the rules, never the caller's own shell -- such libraries commonly `exit 1` during sourcing when a derivation yields nothing, which kills the caller), then counting how many rules' file-half regexes match at least one discovered source path. Report a vacuous pass as a first-class status (pass_vacuous) carrying rules_matched/rules_total, never collapsed into pass.

An advisory wrapper around a fail-closed tool should ALWAYS exit 0 and carry every finding as JSON fields on stdout. A non-zero exit invites a caller to treat the result as a failure, which defeats the advisory contract. Reserve a real non-zero exit for the wrapper's OWN argument errors, and classify the wrapped tool's ambiguous exit codes into distinct named statuses (disambiguating a shared exit code on stderr content before assigning meaning) rather than passing them through.

In a shared fixture test suite where upstream groups install degraded collaborator stubs and never restore them, a new group appended at the end inherits them. A forwarding assertion written as 'flag NOT present in argv' then passes VACUOUSLY when no dispatch was built at all. Install the group's own deterministic stubs AND add a non-vacuity guard that FAILS when the expected argv line is absent, rather than treating absence as a negative result.
